content: Mifepristone interacts with various drugs by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Below are the detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration: 1. Mifepristone and Ritonavir: Mifepristone increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing's syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Mifepristone and Rivaroxaban: Mifepristone increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely due to the risk of increased serum concentrations. 3. Mifepristone and Roflumilast (Topical): Mifepristone elevates roflumilast levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Mifepristone and Romidepsin: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 5. Mifepristone and Rosiglitazone: Mifepristone increases rosiglitazone levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor therapy. 6. Mifepristone and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases mifepristone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 7. Mifepristone and Sacubitril/Valsartan: Mifepristone increases sacubitril/valsartan levels through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Mifepristone and Salmeterol: Mifepristone increases salmeterol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Mifepristone and Saxagliptin: Mifepristone elevates saxagliptin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Mifepristone and Segesterone/Ethinyl Estradiol: Mifepristone decreases the effects of these contraceptives through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use backup contraceptive methods. 11. Mifepristone and Seladelpar: Mifepristone increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 12. Mifepristone and Selegiline: Mifepristone increases selegiline levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor therapy. 13. Mifepristone and Selexipag: Mifepristone increases selexipag levels by reducing its metabolism. Reduce selexipag dose to once daily if co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 14. Mifepristone and Selpercatinib: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Reduce selpercatinib dose and monitor ECGs for QT prolongation. 15. Mifepristone and Sertraline: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 16. Mifepristone and Sitagliptin: Mifepristone increases sitagliptin levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use the smallest recommended doses and monitor therapy. 17. Mifepristone and Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Mifepristone increases levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Mifepristone and Solifenacin: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Mifepristone and Sorafenib: Mifepristone increases sorafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Mifepristone and Sotalol: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 21. Mifepristone and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases mifepristone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 22. Mifepristone and Stiripentol: Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, may alter mifepristone levels. Monitor therapy closely. 23. Mifepristone and Sufentanil: Mifepristone increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce sufentanil dose and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 24. Mifepristone and Sunitinib: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Mifepristone and Tadalafil: Mifepristone increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Mifepristone and Tamoxifen: Mifepristone decreases tamoxifen effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Mifepristone and Tamsulosin: Mifepristone increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Mifepristone and Tasimelteon: Mifepristone increases tasimelteon levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Mifepristone and Tazemetostat: Tazemetostat decreases mifepristone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Mifepristone and Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases mifepristone levels as a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor therapy closely. 31. Mifepristone and Telavancin: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 32. Mifepristone and Temsirolimus: Mifepristone increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Allow a one-week period after discontinuing mifepristone before increasing temsirolimus to its original dose. 33. Mifepristone and Terbinafine: Mifepristone increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Mifepristone and Thiothixene: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 35. Mifepristone and Ticagrelor: Mifepristone increases ticagrelor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Mifepristone and Tinidazole: Mifepristone increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Mifepristone and Tipranavir: Mifepristone increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Mifepristone and Tisotumab Vedotin: Mifepristone increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 39. Mifepristone and Tofacitinib: Mifepristone increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce tofacitinib dose if co-administered with chronic mifepristone therapy. 40. Mifepristone and Toremifene: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 41. Mifepristone and Tramadol: Mifepristone increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 42. Mifepristone and Treprostinil: Mifepristone increases treprostinil levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor therapy. 43. Mifepristone and Tretinoin: Mifepristone increases tretinoin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 44. Mifepristone and Triclabendazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 45. Mifepristone and Trimipramine: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Mifepristone and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Mifepristone increases levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 47. Mifepristone and Upadacitinib: Mifepristone increases upadacitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution, especially with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Mifepristone and Valbenazine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 49. Mifepristone and Valsartan: Mifepristone increases valsartan levels through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 50. Mifepristone and Vamorolone: Mifepristone increases vamorolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients over 50 kg. 51. Mifepristone and Vandetanib: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 52. Mifepristone and Vardenafil: Mifepristone increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce vardenafil dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 53. Mifepristone and Velpatasvir: Mifepristone increases velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 54. Mifepristone and Vemurafenib: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 55. Mifepristone and Venlafaxine: Mifepristone increases venlafaxine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 56. Mifepristone and Verapamil: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 57. Mifepristone and Vilazodone: Mifepristone increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce vilazodone dose to 20 mg/day if intolerable adverse effects occur. 58. Mifepristone and Vinblastine: Mifepristone increases vinblastine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 59. Mifepristone and Vincristine: Mifepristone increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 60. Mifepristone and Vincristine Liposomal: Mifepristone increases vincristine liposomal levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 61. Mifepristone and Vinorelbine: Mifepristone increases vinorelbine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 62. Mifepristone and Voclosporin: Both drugs increase each other’s effects via QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 63. Mifepristone and Vorapaxar: Mifepristone increases vorapaxar levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 64. Mifepristone and Voriconazole: Voriconazole increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing's syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 65. Mifepristone and Vorinostat: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 66. Mifepristone and Vortioxetine: Mifepristone increases vortioxetine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 67. Mifepristone and Zanubrutinib: Mifepristone increases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 68. Mifepristone and Ziprasidone: Co-administration may prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available. 69. Mifepristone and Zolpidem: Mifepristone increases zolpidem levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 70. Mifepristone and Zuranolone: Mifepristone decreases zuranolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
